content.text: SUMMARY

Since life originated on earth nearly 3.8 billion years ago, there had been enormous diversification of life forms on earth. Biodiversity refers to the sum total of diversity that exists at all levels of biological organisation. Of particular importance is the diversity at genetic, species and ecosystem levels and conservation efforts are aimed at protecting diversity at all these levels.
More than 1.5 million species have been recorded in the world, but there might still be nearly 6 million species on earth waiting to be

discovered and named. Of the named species, > 70 per cent are animals, of which 70 per cent are insects. The group Fungi has more species than all the vertebrate species combined. India, with about 45,000 species of plants and twice as many species of animals, is one of the 12 mega diversity countries of the world.

Species diversity on earth is not uniformly distributed but shows interesting patterns. It is generally highest in the tropics and decreases towards the poles. Important explanations for the species richness of the tropics are: Tropics had more evolutionary time; they provide a relatively constant environment and, they receive more solar energy which contributes to greater productivity. Species richness is also function of the area of a region; the species-area relationship is generally a rectangular hyperbolic function.

It is believed that communities with high diversity tend to be less variable, more productive and more resistant to biological invasions. Earth's fossil history reveals incidence of mass extinctions in the past, but the present rates of extinction, largely attributed to human activities, are 100 to 1000 times higher. Nearly 700 species have become extinct in recent times and more than 15,500 species (of which > 650 are from India) currently face the threat of extinction. The causes of high extinction rates at present include habitat (particularly forests) loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, biological invasions and co-extinctions.

content.text: Earth's rich biodiversity is vital for the very survival of mankind. The reasons for conserving biodiversity are narrowly utilitarian, broadly utilitarian and ethical. Protected areas, national parks, wildlife sanctuaries in situ methods hain jahan species natural habitats mein rehti hain.

pyqs.question: In which of the following both pairs have correct combination:  (AIPMT 2015)

options.a: In situ conservation: Cryopreservation    Ex situ conservation: Wildlife Sanctuary
options.b: In situ conservation: Seed Bank    Ex situ conservation: National Park
options.c: In situ conservation: Tissue culture    Ex situ conservation: Sacred groves
options.d: In situ conservation: National Park    Ex situ conservation: Botanical Garden

pyqs.explanation_en: In situ conservation preserves species in their natural habitats, while ex situ conservation maintains them in artificial environments. National Parks are protected natural areas (in situ), and botanical gardens are cultivated plant collections (ex situ). The other options incorrectly pair techniques - cryopreservation and tissue culture are ex situ methods, while sacred groves are in situ conservation.
pyqs.explanation_hi: In situ conservation mein species ko natural habitat mein preserve karte hain, ex situ mein artificial environment mein. National Parks natural protected areas hain (in situ), botanical gardens cultivated plant collections hain (ex situ). Baaki options galat pairing hain - cryopreservation aur tissue culture ex situ methods hain, sacred groves in situ conservation hain.

pyqs.question:
Match the List-I with List-II: (NEET 2022 Phase 2)
List – I
(a) Sacred groves
(b) Zoological park
(c) Nile perch
(d) Amazon forest

List – II
(i) Alien species
(ii) Release of large quantity of oxygen
(iii) Ex-situ conservation
(iv) Khasi Hills in Meghalaya
pyqs.explanation_en: Sacred groves are traditional protected forest patches found in Khasi Hills, Meghalaya (a-iv). Zoological parks are artificial facilities for ex situ conservation (b-iii). Nile perch is an alien species introduced to Lake Victoria causing native fish extinctions (c-i). Amazon rainforest produces approximately 20% of global oxygen, earning it the 'lungs of Earth' title (d-ii).
pyqs.explanation_hi: Sacred groves traditional protected forest patches hain jo Khasi Hills, Meghalaya mein milte hain (a-iv). Zoological parks artificial facilities hain ex situ conservation ke liye (b-iii). Nile perch alien species hai jo Lake Victoria mein introduce hui aur native fish species extinct kar diya (c-i). Amazon rainforest global oxygen ka 20% produce karta hai isliye 'lungs of Earth' kehlaata hai (d-ii).

pyqs.question: Which one of the following is not a method of in situ conservation of biodiversity? (NEET 2019)
pyqs.explanation_en: In situ conservation maintains species within their natural habitats and ecosystems. Sacred groves, biosphere reserves, and wildlife sanctuaries all represent natural or semi-natural areas where native species are protected in their original environment. Botanical gardens are artificially maintained plant collections where species are cultivated outside their natural habitat, making them ex situ conservation facilities.
pyqs.explanation_hi: In situ conservation mein species ko unke natural habitats aur ecosystems mein maintain karte hain. Sacred groves, biosphere reserves, wildlife sanctuaries ye sab natural ya semi-natural areas hain jahan native species ko original environment mein protect karte hain. Botanical gardens artificial plant collections hain jahan species ko natural habitat ke bahar cultivate karte hain - ye ex situ conservation hai.

pyqs.question: An example of ex situ conservation is:  (AIPMT 2014)
pyqs.explanation_en: Ex situ conservation involves preserving genetic material or species outside their natural habitat under controlled conditions. Seed banks store seeds of various plant species at controlled temperature and humidity to maintain genetic diversity for future use. National parks, wildlife sanctuaries, and sacred groves are all in situ conservation methods where species remain in natural environments.
pyqs.explanation_hi: Ex situ conservation mein genetic material ya species ko natural habitat ke bahar controlled conditions mein preserve karte hain. Seed banks mein various plant species ke seeds ko controlled temperature aur humidity mein store karte hain genetic diversity maintain karne ke liye. National parks, wildlife sanctuaries, sacred groves ye sab in situ methods hain jahan species natural environment mein rehti hain.
